### Observed differences

- A17 is no longer executed. In the earlier window it ran in about 53 in 100 traces (105 of 200), on average about 3.7 times per trace containing it, around the middle of the trace (median relative position about 0.64), with its outgoing transitions going almost only to A15 (about 53%) and A14 (about 46%). In the later window no trace contains A17, and neither its outgoing transitions nor its positions are observed. [OCC013, DIR017, POS006]

- A01 is newly executed. In the earlier window no trace contains A01; in the later window about 39 in 100 traces (77 of 200) contain it, always at most once, around the middle of the trace (median relative position about 0.45). Its observed outgoing transitions go mainly to A09 (about 27%), A07 (about 23%) and A12 (about 19%). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001]

- A01 is integrated into the existing flow, while A17's integration is gone. Earlier, A02, A12, A14 and A15 always occurred without A01; later, A01 co-occurs with A02 in about 39 in 100 traces (always after or interleaved with A02), with A12 and A15 in about 19 in 100, and with A14 in about 11 in 100, and A02, A03, A04, A07, A09 and A11 all show new transitions into A01. Conversely, A17's earlier co-occurrences with A02, A12 and A15 (about 53 in 100 each) and with A14 (about 30 in 100) all fell to zero. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR007, DIR009, DIR011, REL009, REL012, REL014, REL015]

- A12 rerouted: its outgoing transitions previously went to A17 (about 52%) and A16 (about 47%); in the later window they go to A16 (about 44%), A15 (about 29%) and A14 (about 22%), i.e., the share that previously went to A17 now goes to A15 and A14. [DIR012]

- A01 and A17 were never seen together: earlier the choice was A17 without A01 (about 53 in 100) or neither (about 48 in 100); later it is A01 without A17 (about 39 in 100) or neither (about 62 in 100). [REL005]

- Two other activities are executed less often: A06 in about 52 → 31 in 100 traces and A08 in about 47 → 30 in 100; A12 and A16 also repeat somewhat less (A12 mean 3.7 → 3.2 occurrences per trace, A16 1.8 → 1.4). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC008, OCC012]

- Event-position gaps between A12, A14 and A15 shrank (for example A12→A15 and A12→A14 now occur most often one step apart instead of two, A15→A15 three instead of four), and A13's outgoing traffic moved from mainly A02 (about 42%) to a spread over A10, A01, A06 and A05 (about 21–26% each), the latter based on only about 19 observed outgoing transitions per window. [LAG007, LAG008, LAG011, LAG012, LAG015, LAG016, DIR013]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A17 was removed from the process while A01 was added as a new activity in the middle of the flow. Earlier, A17 ran nearly four times per trace in which it appeared, in roughly half of all cases, mainly after A12 and before A14/A15; in the later window it is unobserved in 200 traces, its edges to A14/A15 and its positions are gone, and its co-occurrences with A02, A12, A14 and A15 dropped to zero. Over the same window A01, previously unobserved, now runs once in about 39 in 100 traces around mid-trace, receives new transitions from A02, A03, A04, A07, A09 and A11, leads mainly to A09, A07 and A12, and A12's traffic that previously went to A17 now goes to A15 and A14. [OCC013, OCC001, DIR017, DIR001, DIR012, POS006, POS001, REL005, REL009, REL012, REL014, REL015, REL001]

The support is direct and consistent: both changes appear in occurrence, routing, position and relation indicators alike, with magnitudes (105 of 200 → 0 of 200; 0 of 200 → 77 of 200) whose differences exceed those seen in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data, so sampling fluctuation or a rare variant surfacing cannot plausibly explain them. Limitations: zero participation shows non-observation rather than proven removal, and because A01's main successors (A09, A07, A12) differ from A17's (A15, A14), the evidence cannot establish whether A01 took over A17's role or whether the two are independent addition and removal; the agreeing items also largely re-describe the same two trace-level changes rather than constituting independent confirmations. [OCC013, OCC001, DIR017, DIR001, DIR012, REL005]

Other differences: A06 and A08 are executed in clearly fewer traces (about 52 → 31 and 47 → 30 in 100), A12 and A16 repeat somewhat less, and position gaps among A12, A14 and A15 tightened — plausibly side effects of the same restructuring, but nothing in the evidence ties them directly to the A17/A01 changes. A13's rerouting towards A01 rests on about 19 observations per window and remains weak. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC008, OCC012, LAG007, LAG008, LAG015, LAG016, DIR013]
